Class NitriteIndexManagement

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.data.nitrite.operations.NitriteIndexManagement
public final class NitriteIndexManagement extends Object
Manages indexes for one Micronaut Data Nitrite datasource.

This is the provider boundary for index DDL. Applications identify a collection and its persisted field by name, while all Nitrite API types and index options remain inside the Micronaut Data adapter. Operations are intentionally idempotent where possible so a failed or interrupted rebuild can be retried on the next run.

Index DDL is not part of a Nitrite data transaction, so an index dropped for the duration of a bulk load is not restored by rolling that load back. dropUniqueIndex(String, String) returns an NitriteIndexManagement.IndexScope for that case: it rebuilds the index when the scope closes, whether the work inside it succeeded or threw.

Since:
5.2.0

    • rebuildUniqueIndex

      public void rebuildUniqueIndex(String collectionName, String fieldName)
      Rebuilds a unique index on a single field in one database-side index build.

      If an index already exists, it is dropped first so this method guarantees that the resulting index is unique rather than merely leaving an existing index untouched.

      Parameters:
      collectionName - the Nitrite collection name
      fieldName - the persisted field indexed by Nitrite

    • dropUniqueIndex

      public NitriteIndexManagement.IndexScope dropUniqueIndex(String collectionName, String fieldName)
      Drops an existing unique index and returns a scope that rebuilds it when closed.

      If the index was not present when this method starts, the scope is a no-op. This preserves the datasource's create-indexes=false configuration while still making the normal indexed case safe across exceptions.

      Parameters:
      collectionName - the Nitrite collection name
      fieldName - the persisted field indexed by Nitrite
      Returns:
      a closeable scope that restores the index if it was present
